To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dynamic compression of mouse chondrocyes cultured in agarose induces a rapid activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase and a down-regulation of gene transcription of type II procollage.
we developed a protocol to culture mouse chondroctyes in agarose, which allows to analyze the effect of dynamic compression on gene expression and phosphorylation state.
we have developed protocols that allow the analysis of the molecular response of murine chandrocytes to dynamic compression in agarose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model system that can be used to study the effect of dynamic compression on chondrocytic mechanosensing.
the development of an in vitro model system for studying the molecular mechanisms of chondroctytes mechanotransduction.

the development of new protocols for the analysis of the response of chondroctyes to mechanical loading, and the application of these protocols to the study of molecular mechanisms involved in mechanotrasduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this model system can be considered as an appropriate model for mechanobiology studies of cartilagous tissue.
the chondrocytic/agarose system is a valuable tool to study the effect of dynamic compression on the expression of genes involved in chondroblast differentiation.
this model system can be used to study chondrocytic mechanotransduction and the role of matrix proteins, transmembrane receptors and signalling molecules in response to mechanical stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the chondrocytic/agarose constructs, cultured and compressed as described, are a valuable model system to explore the molecular basis of mechanotransducion in chondroctyes, and that the Flexcell® system is an efficient tool to study this phenomenon.
the chondrocytic response to mechanical stimulation is mediated by MAPKs and involves transcriptional regulation of the genes coding for cFos and type II procollage, but not for type I procollagen.
chondrocytic response to mechanical loading is mediated by MAPKs activation and involves the regulation of gene transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse model is an interesting alternative to study the role played by the pericellular matrix in mechanotransducion.
chondrocytic mechanotransduction can be studied in vitro in the chondrocyt/agarose model using dynamic compression.
chondrocyt/agarose constructs, prepared and characterized as described, are well suited for studying mechanotransduction and the role of matrix in this phenomenon.
